speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand what is causing this, I need to ask you a few questions: Do you have a family history of easy bleeding or bruising, and do you experience excessive bleeding after cuts, dental work, or vaccinations?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The presentation of petechiae on the distal extremities, mucous membrane bleeding, and bruising in a 4-year-old male is classic for ITP; I have diagnosed you based on this clinical evidence.
